look_here_first: START WITH THE LEAVES: common ragweed is an ANNUAL with finely divided, fernlike leaves, usually opposite low on the stem and alternate above. NEXT inspect flowering stems: dangling greenish MALE pollen heads form terminal spikes; much smaller FEMALE heads sit below them near the upper leaf axils. FINALLY check the mature fruit: a small woody bur with several short pointed projections. Western ragweed can have similar flowers and divided leaves but is a perennial spreading from underground rhizomes; check connected stems if uncertain.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Annual from seed; does not produce a persistent network of perennial underground rhizomes. An established western ragweed patch may have multiple stems connected belowground.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Erect, branching herb of disturbed ground.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Lower leaves opposite, upper leaves alternate; blades generally deeply once- or twice-divided into narrow lobes. Examine leaf position along the same stem rather than one isolated leaf.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Small drooping male pollen-bearing heads arranged along terminal spikes, with tiny separate female heads below in the upper leaf axils. Both sexes occur on the same plant.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Female heads mature into small woody burrlike involucres with usually 4–7 short spines or projections; photograph mature fruit beside a ruler.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Annual plant with opposite lower leaves, alternate upper leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Dangling male heads in terminal spikes; small female heads beneath

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small woody fruit with short crownlike projections
